title: How far does the car go on this much petrol?
description: A car runs sixteen kilometres on one litre of petrol, and the petrol is two and three quarters of a litre. The mixed number becomes a fraction, and the multiplication is shortened by cancelling the common factor four.
teaching_notes: One idea: turn the mixed number into a fraction, then multiply by the distance for one litre and cancel before multiplying. Watch for students who multiply only the whole part two and leave out the three quarters.

source: Figure it Out (problems with fractions): a car runs 16 km using 1 litre of petrol. How far will it go using 2 3/4 litres of petrol?
video_script.why: A learner writes a mixed number as a fraction, as with the area of the bricks, and multiplies it by the distance for one litre.
video_script.substitution: the book's own car that runs sixteen kilometres on one litre
video_script.anchor: a car that runs sixteen kilometres on every litre of petrol
video_script.payoff_line: The car goes forty four kilometres.
video_script.fraction_reading: two and three quarters, eleven quarters
maths_rules: check: 2 x 16 = 32 and 3 x 16 = 48, and 44 lies between 32 and 48
video_script.design: A road marked in sixteen kilometre steps, one for each litre; the last litre is only three quarters used.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a car on a road with a fuel can of two and three quarters of a litre

marks.run: the car moves along the road for one litre
marks.ask: the fuel can of two and three quarters litres appears

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a car.
<bookmark mark='run'/>The car runs sixteen kilometres using one litre of petrol.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How far will it go using two and three quarters litres of petrol?

beats.on_screen: the car and the road stay on the board; Keeko sits beside the road

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a road in steps of sixteen kilometres; two full litres and a three quarter litre marked on it

marks.steps: each litre is a step of sixteen kilometres
marks.part: the last step is only three quarters of a litre
marks.mixed: two and three quarters is split into quarters

narration: <bookmark mark='steps'/>Every litre of petrol carries the car sixteen kilometres.
<bookmark mark='part'/>Two and three quarters litres is two full litres and a part of a third.
<bookmark mark='mixed'/>As in your book, a mixed number can be written as one fraction.

beats.on_screen: Given: 16 km on 1 litre; petrol 2 3/4 litres

marks.given: the distance for one litre and the petrol are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the car runs sixteen kilometres on one litre, and uses two and three quarters litres.

beats.on_screen: To find: the distance on 2 3/4 litres
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how far the car goes.
<bookmark mark='mixed'/>Step one, write two and three quarters as a fraction, two times four plus three over four.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>That is eleven quarters of a litre.

marks.times: sixteen times eleven quarters is written
marks.over: the product is written over four

narration: <bookmark mark='times'/>Step two, the distance is sixteen times the petrol, because each litre gives sixteen kilometres.

marks.cancel: sixteen and four are cancelled by the common factor four

narration: <bookmark mark='cancel'/>Step three, cancel the common factor four from sixteen and the denominator four.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Sixteen over four is four, which leaves four times eleven.

marks.check: the distances for two litres and three litres are written

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the size. Two litres give thirty two kilometres, and three litres give forty eight.
Our answer must lie between them.

marks.ans: the answer is boxed and placed between thirty two and forty eight

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The car goes forty four kilometres.
That lies between thirty two and forty eight, as it should.
